title: Dabble Me: a simple, private journal that helps you write.
pitch: A journal built for people and their agents: WebMCP tools search, open, and draft journal entries in your signed-in session. Work with the agent to write your entry and submit it together.
about_excerpt: A journal built for people and their agents: WebMCP tools search, open, and draft journal entries in your signed-in session. Work with the agent to write your entry and submit it together. Like Comment Story Updates Drafting a new journal entry for the day. Utilizing the search function. Inspiration I built Dabble Me in 2014 after OhLife shut down . I had been a near-daily user for three years. The trick was that the medium was email: a prompt arrived in my inbox, I replied, and the habit stuck. No extra app or thumbs-only typing. No notification fatigue. It was designed precisely for my sick desire to constantly need Inbox Zero. Dogfooding this app has become my sacred space now: the first dates with my now wife, photos and how I felt seeing my boys grow up, and the personal growth I would've otherwise missed had I not read how far I've come. The daily email bring these private days back to me, the way Timehop does for public posts. What it does Dabble Me is a live, private journal. You can still write by replying to email. PRO users can also search, reflect, and draft in the browser. With WebMCP enabled , a signed-in tab registers structured tools: search_journal_entries / list_journal_entries / analyze_journal — read this session’s journal only open_journal_day / open_search_page / open_write_page — move the UI so the person sees the same screen draft_journal_entry — fill the write form and highlight it get_journal_session — tell the agent whether the tab is signed in and whether PRO tools are available Signup, login, search, and write forms also use declarative toolname / tooldescription attributes so an agent can fill fields without guessing labels. A status banner on the page makes the agent’s action visible. How we built it The product was already a Rails app with a remote, OAuth MCP server at /mcp . WebMCP is a different layer: tools run in the page, with the user’s cookie session, not a headless API token. Discovery so a client that only has https://dabble.me can find the surface: /.well-known/webmcp , /mcp/server-card , /.well-known/ai-catalog.json , plus Link headers and /llms.txt Session JSON at /webmcp/journal/* that reuses the same search/list/analyze logic as remote MCP, always scoped to current_user public/webmcp.js that feature-detects document.modelContext (and the older navigator.modelContext ), registers tools for the current auth state, fills Summernote on draft, and navigates for “open this day” Declarative forms for account and journal UI, without toolautosubmit Challenges we ran into The biggest challenge was privacy vs. demo-ability. Journal apps cannot run anonymously. They also cannot require WebAuthn if we want an in-app browser to finish login. The compromise: session cookies, PRO for write/search, and a dedicated demo account...not a real diary. The second was editors. The write box is Summernote, not a plain <textarea> . A declarative form fill would look done and still leave the rich editor empty. draft_journal_entry has to talk to the editor, then leave Create Entry for the human. Accomplishments that we're proud of This is not a toy journal. Dabble Me has been a real, private, email-first product since the OhLife shutdown in 2014. The agent and the user share one interface. When the agent searches or drafts, the page shows it. Writes are cooperative by construction: fill and highlight so the draft is reviewed by a human before submitting ai-only entries. We kept two complementary layers honest: remote MCP for ChatGPT/Claude connectors, WebMCP for the live tab. What we learned WebMCP is not “MCP in a JSON file.” It is a browser API for this document, this session, this user . Discovery helps agents find you. registerTool + execute is what they actually call. We also learned that the best tool for a journal is often the one that refuses to finish. Submission should be human-reviewed...a feature, not a bug. 😁 What's next for Dabble Me More page-state tools: jump to a hashtag, open last year on this day, draft into an existing date the way email replies already append Tighter visual feedback when a tool is running ( toolchange , :tool-form-active ) A first-class “agent draft” review state so a filled form is obvious even after a refresh Keep the remote MCP server for headless clients, and keep WebMCP for the tab where the human is sitting Built With javascript ruby-on-rails Try it out dabble.me Created by Paul Arterburn Like Share this project: Updates Paul Arterburn started this project — Aug 25, 2026 07:32 PM EDT
